steps: Open Bitbucket.
Browse or search public repositories.
Open a repository and inspect source, commits, branches, downloads, and project metadata.
Apply an impossible search and return to repositories.
Open sign in.
Sign in with a seeded local developer account.
Open dashboard, profile, and account history.
Sign out.
Create a repository with description, visibility, README, ignore template, and license.
Refresh and verify persistence.
Create or edit a file and commit it.
Create a branch and switch to it.
Compare the branch with main.
Verify the commit and branch persist.
Create an issue with labels, assignee, and milestone.
Comment and close it.
Open a pull request between branches.
Inspect the diff, add a reviewer and comment, then update status.
Open pipelines.
Inspect a run, job status, and logs.
Retry the deterministic local run without contacting a runner.
Add an existing local member and select a role.
Change topics, default branch, notifications, visibility, or archive state.
Verify a user without permission receives access denied.
Inspect HTTPS, Sourcetree, VS Code, and download options.
Fork a public repository into the local workspace.
Verify repository history remains local.
Inspect registration and password-recovery entry surfaces without sending email.
Submit an empty action and inspect validation.
Open a missing deep link and return to repository discovery.
Open support guidance without exposing private data.
